newsitem.title: CHINA: China mulls mine closures to cut tungsten output.
newsitem.headline: China mulls mine closures to cut tungsten output.

text.p: China is considering halting production at some state-owned tungsten mines to reduce output, an official with the China National Non-ferrous Metals Import and Export Corp said on Thursday.
"It is possible...some state-owned mines will be asked to halt production. It could happen this year or in 1997," the official said. He offered no details.
Tungsten prices have plunged in recent years due to oversupply in the world market.
China is the world's largest producer of tungsten, a metal used mainly to make carbide tools and special steel for the automobile and construction industries.
China hosted an international tungsten conference last week, drawing delegates from major producing countries such as China, Russia, the United States, Portugal and Vietnam.
Participants agreed that the mining industry had serious problems that needed to be addressed, according to a statement issued by the conference organisers.

The problems were mainly created by a massive fall in consumption in Russia since 1991, coupled with oversupply in the international market due to large releases from stockpiles in Russia, Kazakhstan and China, it said.
The situation has been made worse by an increase in private Chinese mines and the threat of further stockpile releases from some major producing countries, it said.
Tungsten prices have fallen well below operating costs for most mines, the conference statement said.

The statement said that delegates from China, Russia and the United States would petition their respective governments for suspension of stockpile releases until the tungsten mining industry has recovered.
Delegates agreed that worldwide tungsten mine production capacity would decline substantially in the near future because of weak demand, it said.
China has already reduced concentrates production in large and medium-size tungsten mines this year because of depressed prices, it said.
